key_findings: A: with no encryption, the evidence, the password and the session token are all readable in the capture.

B: the evidence is unreadable even without TLS, because the file is encrypted in the browser before it is sent. The password and session token are still visible over plain HTTP, so TLS is still needed.
C: with TLS added, none of the markers can be found: user names, file name, password and token are hidden too. Negotiated TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.
how_to: Wireshark: File > Open, choose a .pcap from report/captures/
Follow a stream: right click a packet > Follow > TCP Stream
Display filters: http.request.method == "POST"   |   tls.handshake.type == 1   |   frame contains "alice"
To decode the plain HTTP captures: Analyze > Decode As... > TCP port > HTTP (use the port in the report)
